cells.tense: Right now what you have long tended is shining through, and you are here at the open door under the pen.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Look back over the last few times this work carried itself without pushing, and trace the one pattern running through them — what you actually did each time.
cells.core:
When the work is finished, the light in it is not effort anymore. It comes off what was tended, not off the person holding it, and you can stand at the door and watch it hold. People who keep hauling light forward wear down; you have put enough in that it stands by itself now, and what it throws is wider than anything you could push.

The pull is still there, some direction you recognize and didn't need to be shown. Look back over the last few times this carried itself and find the one line running through them. That line will show you the next place it works. Then set this one down, with your hands open, which is how completion opens instead of closing.
cells.sheetLine: What you tended carries its own light now. Stand in the doorway and watch it hold.
cells.verb: to follow a light you didn't have to be shown, and hand what was finished forward
cells.place: at the open door where this work is complete and the next has not begun

cells.tense: Ahead of you the light is being thrown onto a future that hasn't been written yet, and faster than it can arrive.
cells.act: sit with not knowing for ten minutes instead of filling it
cells.ask: Sit for ten minutes with what you don't know about how this will land, and don't fill the silence with how bright it will be.
cells.core:
Every good thing you speak of comes out in a slight key of hurry, and that brightness dazzles more than it lights the road. It reads as optimism from the outside. From inside it's the opposite of waiting — you are projecting forward because stopping would leave you sitting next to something you can't see yet.

The direction is still right. Ten minutes with the not-knowing, without filling it, will show you that. Then begin with the one part that matters, and leave the rest until it asks. The shine that lands comes from what is actually here, not from what you have told yourself is coming.
cells.sheetLine: You're lighting a future you haven't arrived at yet. Let the dark stay dark a while.
cells.verb: to follow a light you didn't have to be shown, and hand what was finished forward
cells.place: at the open door where this work is complete and the next has not begun

cells.tense: You planted and kept planting, and hope went flat a long time ago, and you are still standing at this door.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Pick the quietest living piece of this and give it ten minutes today — no result asked of it, nothing depending on it.
cells.core:
There is still a doorway here, and you are standing in it without much light coming through. What is underneath is not laziness; it's a long run of tending that didn't flower, and anyone stops feeding something that doesn't answer, the whole self pulling back. The pull is still in you — it went quiet, not away.

Don't try to restore the glow or force a result. Give the smallest living piece what it needs today, ten minutes, asking nothing back. Tending a young thing without demanding what it becomes is how the warmth returns — not through more effort, through a lighter hand.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing flowered and you stopped expecting it. Tend one living piece anyway.
cells.verb: to follow a light you didn't have to be shown, and hand what was finished forward
cells.place: at the open door where this work is complete and the next has not begun

cells.tense: The light is on and you're saying it's the room's, and you can't see whose hand is on the switch.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: Next time someone treats what you built as smaller than it is, don't argue and don't shrink it — keep it the size it actually is.
cells.core:
People leave your presence lighter and you'd say that's just how it happens, and you may not know your own light is on. It's been on for a while; this is not new for you. Or it went down so gradually that nothing marks the change, and either way you're describing the room while standing in it with your hand on the switch.

You don't need to own the whole thing. Just hold its shape at its true size the next time someone asks you to make it smaller. You started doing this before anyone told you it was worth watching, and it has been worth watching the whole time. Keep it the size it is.
cells.sheetLine: The light is on. You keep saying it must be the room.
cells.verb: to follow a light you didn't have to be shown, and hand what was finished forward

attempts.check: The claimed read is that what has been cultivated now shines on its own, and the remedy is to trace the mechanism underneath rather than the finished thing; the record supports the shine and the pattern-medicine but not that the person is at peace with finishing. A reader could reasonably say they are not glowing at all, only bracing for the next thing, which would make the Balanced cell wrong about them. The ask survives that error because tracing a pattern that already works is useful whether or not they feel radiant. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line that says they have arrived.
